items.statement: D is the quaternion algebra over F ramified exactly at Σ ∪ S_∞ (possible by (11)–(12)); H_D(U) is the space of O-valued automorphic forms on (D ⊗ A_F^∞)^× of level U; U₀ = ∏ U_{0,v} (Iwahori at Σ, maximal elsewhere), U₀(Q) and U₁(Q; N) are the Taylor–Wiles levels; T_D is the Hecke algebra, m_D, m_{D,Q} its maximal ideals of r̄; H_D carries the twists f ⊗ χ by quadratic characters (p = 2) and the torsion exponent m_D of [KW09, §7.2].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. The standard quaternionic setting of Kisin and Khare–Wintenberger: R22.1 constructs 'the localised finite-level Hecke module and algebra with the required local type', R22.2 the Taylor–Wiles levels and the p = 2 twisting.

items.name: Minkowski: Q has no everywhere unramified extension
items.statement: Every number field K ≠ Q is ramified at some rational prime. The paper uses the consequence that the Galois group Γ_π = Gal(K̃_π/Q) is generated by its inertia subgroups at finite primes (their normal closure fixes an everywhere unramified extension of Q).
items.locator: Completion of the proof of Theorem 5.5, arXiv v2 p. 42
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Read at Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ExistsRamified.lean (blob d68374b4): exists_not_isUnramifiedIn gives a prime p not unramified in 𝒪_K when finrank ℚ K ≠ 1, and finrank_eq_one_of_unramified is its contrapositive. The inertia-generation step is the one-line deduction stated, used in all-coefficient-conjugates-tensor.

items.name: The BLGGT relation ρ_v ∼ ρ′_v
items.statement: For a finite place v and continuous ρ_v, ρ′_v : G_{F_v} → GL_n(Z̄_p), potentially crystalline if v | p, ρ_v ∼ ρ′_v ('ρ_v connects to ρ′_v', [BLGGT14, §1.3–1.4]) means their reductions agree and they define points on a common irreducible component of a suitable (fixed-type, and at v | p fixed Hodge type) lifting ring. For ρ, ρ′ : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) with irreducible residual representations, ρ|G_{F_v} ∼ ρ′|G_{F_v} means the relation for integral conjugates. It implies equality of the restrictions (r|_I, N) of the Weil–Deligne representations ([BLGGT14, Remark (6), p. 524]).
items.locator: §1.2, arXiv v2 p. 7 (used in Lemma 3.1(5), Lemma 5.6, Theorem 5.9)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. As item 58 of PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B, routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Potentially diagonalisable representations
items.statement: A potentially crystalline ρ : G_K → GL_n(Z̄_p) (K/Q_p finite) is potentially diagonalisable if after restriction to some finite extension it connects (∼) to a sum of crystalline characters ([BLGGT14, §1.4]). Ordinary and Fontaine–Laffaille representations (K/Q_p unramified, Hodge–Tate weights in an interval of length < p − 1) are potentially diagonalisable ([BLGGT14, Lemma 1.4.3]), and so are potentially Barsotti–Tate representations ([GK14, Lemma 4.4.1]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. As item 59 of PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B, routed to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Algebraic-group facts in the proof of Lemma 2.2
items.statement: Over Q̄_p: a connected reductive subgroup of GL₂ acting irreducibly is SL₂ or GL₂; PGL₂(Q̄_p) is simple as an abstract group, so a subgroup of PGL₂(Q̄_p) × PGL₂(Q̄_p) surjecting onto both factors is the product or the graph of an automorphism; a homomorphism of algebraic groups in characteristic 0 that is bijective on Q̄_p-points is an isomorphism; every automorphism of PGL₂ is inner; Sym^m ⊗ Sym^{m′} is irreducible for SL₂ × SL₂.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2, arXiv v2 p. 10
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Not covered by zariski-closure-image or goursat-lemma. Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 have Goursat's lemma for abstract groups but none of these statements about linear algebraic groups.

items.name: Twisting a RAECSDC representation to a RACSDC one
items.statement: [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4]: for a CM field F and a RAECSDC π of GL_n(A_F) (π^∨ ≅ π^c ⊗ (χ∘N∘det)), there is an algebraic Hecke character ψ of F such that π ⊗ (ψ∘det) is RACSDC; the paper also uses it to construct the characters X, Y of Theorem 4.1(15).
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 4.1 (p. 26) and Theorem 6.5 (p. 51), citing [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. AG2.2: 'For essentially conjugate self-dual forms, carry the algebraic twisting char[acters]'.

items.name: Automorphy of a tensor product does not depend on ι
items.statement: Let π₁, σ be RAESDC with r_{π₁,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} irreducible for one (p, ι). If it is automorphic, then r_{π₁,ȷ} ⊗ r_{σ,ȷ} is automorphic for every prime q and every ȷ : Q̄_q → C (conjugating the automorphic representation by ȷι^{−1} as in Lemma 5.2 and comparing Frobenius traces).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.8 ('cf. Lemma 2.1') and completion of Theorem 5.5, arXiv v2 pp. 42–44
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Used implicitly; Lemma 2.1 covers only symmetric powers. AG2.6 owns coefficient-prime comparison.

items.name: The rank d₀ by class field theory
items.statement: With Δ, Δ₀ and T_{F₂} as in Lemma 3.4(4), d_{0,F₂} equals the Z_p-rank of the anti-invariant part of the closure of O_{K₂,T_{F₂}}^× in ∏_{v|p} O_{K₂,v}^×(p), and it is at least the corresponding rank over K₁.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.4, arXiv v2 p. 17 ('repeating part of the proof of [Tho15, Theorem 7.1]')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Routed with maire-antiunits to the restricted-ramification layer R02.3.

items.name: The auxiliary data v_a, M, X₀, K₀, u₀ of §3
items.statement: Fix v_a satisfying Lemma 3.3. M is the extension of F(ζ_p) cut out by r̄_{π,ι}. X₀ is a finite set of prime-to-p places where π is unramified, containing v_a, such that every Galois subextension M/M′/F of degree > 1 has a place of X₀ that does not split in M′. An extension L/F is X₀-split if every place of X₀ splits completely in L; then L and M are linearly disjoint over F. K₀ is an imaginary quadratic field in which p and the residue characteristics of X₀ ∪ {v₀} split, and u₀ | p is a place of K₀.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: The polarized representation s and the sets of §3
items.statement: After conjugation and enlarging E, s = (r_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι})|G_{K₁} ⊗ y^{1−r} takes values in GL_n(O) and extends to s : G_{F₁} → 𝒢_n(O) with ν ∘ s = ε^{1−n}δ^n_{K₁/F₁} ([BLGGT14, §1.1] for multipliers of tensor products). S_{p,F₁} is the set of p-adic places of F₁, T_{F₁} (resp. T′_{F₁}) the places above v₀ (resp. v_a), S_{F₁} = S_{p,F₁} ∪ T_{F₁}, and S̃_{F₁} a choice of one place ṽ of K₁ above each v ∈ S_{F₁}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. The multiplier sign was checked with the CHT convention: ν(c) = −1 for both parities of r, which equals ε^{1−n}(c).

items.name: s is a lift of type 𝒮_{F₁}
items.statement: The representation s : G_{F₁} → 𝒢_n(O) is a lift of s̄ of type 𝒮_{F₁}: it is ordinary at v | p, of inertial type τ_s at T_{F₁}, has multiplier ε^{1−n}δ^n_{K₁/F₁}, and is unramified outside S_{F₁}. Hence it defines the homomorphism f : R_{𝒮_{F₁}} → O of the final step of Theorem 3.2.
items.locator: Final step of the proof of Theorem 3.2, arXiv v2 p. 25
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. The paper uses this without proof. Unramifiedness outside S_{F₁} needs BC_{F₁/F}(σ) as well as BC_{F₁/F}(π) unramified away from pv₀, which §3 does not arrange (sourceIssues E22). It follows from Lemma 3.1(5), since ∼ preserves (r|_I, N).

items.name: Residual automorphy of the constituents of s̄
items.statement: The irreducible constituents of s̄|G_{K₂} (twists of Sym^r r̄_{σ,ι} and Sym^{r−2} r̄_{σ,ι}) have ι-ordinary automorphic lifts that are Steinberg at ṽ₂: apply a level-raising theorem for GL₂ at v₂ (q_{v₂} ≡ 1 mod p, r̄ trivial there), then take symmetric powers using SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1}. This is a hypothesis of [Tho24, Theorem 6.11] in Proposition 3.9.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.9, arXiv v2 p. 21
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Stated in one sentence without a reference.

items.name: The finite set 𝒫 of generic primes
items.statement: 𝒫 is a finite set of generic primes of R_{𝒮′_{F₂}} of dimension 1 and characteristic p such that every edge Q̄–Q̄′ of the graph of Proposition 3.10 is witnessed by some 𝔭 ∈ 𝒫, and every minimal prime Q of R_{𝒮_{F₁}} lies in a generic 𝔭 with 𝔭_{F₂} ∈ 𝒫. It exists by Propositions 3.10 and 3.11, [Tho15, Proposition 5.3] and the splitting of the p-adic places of F₁ in F₂.
items.locator: §3 between Propositions 3.11 and 3.12, arXiv v2 pp. 22–23
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: The comparison diagram of §3
items.statement: There are Λ_{F₃}-algebra maps R_{𝒮_{F₃}} → R_{𝒮′_{F₂}} and R_{𝒮_{F₃}} → R_{𝒮_{F₁}} (restrictions of lifts of type 𝒮′_{F₂} or 𝒮_{F₁} to G_{F₃} are of type 𝒮_{F₃}: τ_s becomes unipotent because BC_{F₂/F}(π) is unramified above v₀), compatible maps of the subalgebras P, and T_{F₃} → T_{F₂} by soluble base change ([Tho15, Proposition 4.18], [NT21a, Lemma 6.7]). Consequently J_{𝒮_{F₃}}·P_{𝒮′_{F₂}} ⊂ J_{𝒮′_{F₂}}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: The hypotheses of Theorem 5.5 (context S5-global)
items.statement: F totally real, p ≥ 5, 0 < r < p, SP_{r−1}, SP_r and SP_{r+1}, ι : Q̄_p → C, and π RAESDC on GL₂(A_F) with: (1) det r_{π,ι} = ε^{−1}; (2) weight 0 and π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg for every v | p; (3) a place v₀ with q_{v₀} ≡ −1 mod p and π_{v₀} tamely dihedral of order p; (4) for every prime l and every ι_l, r̄_{π,ι_l}(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{l^a}) for some l^a > max(4r, 5), and r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}) with a > a₀(p); (5) π_v potentially unramified for every finite v ∤ p. φ_p ∈ G_{Q_p} is an arithmetic Frobenius lift.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. Eight items cite the context S5-global; this item states it.

items.name: The hypotheses of Theorem 5.9 (context S5-local)
items.statement: F totally real, p ≥ 5, M > p^{a₀(p)}, 0 < r < p, ι, and π RAESDC on GL₂(A_F) with (1)–(3) of S5-global; (4) a place v₁ with q_{v₁} ≡ 1 mod p and π_{v₁} an unramified twist of Steinberg; (5) π_v potentially unramified for every v ∤ pv₁; (6) primes t₁, t₂ > M and places w₁, w₂ of residue characteristics p₁, p₂ > 3 unramified in F, with π_{w_i} tamely dihedral of order t_i and p₁, p₂, t₁, t₂ distinct; (7) with H the ray class field of modulus (8)·∞ and S the places v ≠ w₁, w₂ where π_v is ramified, v is ramified over Q, or v has residue characteristic 2 or 3: w₁ splits in H·F(S) and w₂ splits in H·F(S ∪ {w₁}).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: The CM representations π_K, π′_K, σ_K and T of §4
items.statement: π_K = BC_{K/F}(π), π′_K = BC_{K/F}(π′) and σ_K = BC_{K/F}(σ) ⊗ X^{−1} are RACSDC, and T is the RACSDC representation of GL_n(A_K) of weight 0 with r_{T,ι} ≅ r_{π_K,ι} ⊗ r_{σ_K,ι} ⊗ r_{Y,ι}^{1−r}. Here XX^c = χ∘N and YY^c = |·|_K give r_T^c ≅ r_T^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2r}, and X^{−1}Y^{1−r} has trivial infinity type. The integral models r, r′, s over O with r̄ = r̄′, and the group determinants t, t′ of (r ⊗ s)|G_K ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r},ι} and its π′ analogue, with common reduction t̄.
items.locator: §4 after the reductions, arXiv v2 pp. 27–28
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: Unitary automorphic forms of §4
items.statement: G is the definite unitary group over F with G(R) = {g ∈ M_n(O_K ⊗ R) : g = (1 ⊗ c)(g)^{−t}} for R an O_F-algebra; H_G(V) is the space of O-valued automorphic forms of level V; V₀ = ∏_{v∈Σ} ι_ṽ^{−1}(Iw_ṽ) × ∏_{v∉Σ} G(O_{F_v}), V₀(Q) and V₁(Q; N) (with quotient Δ′_Q/(p^N)) the Taylor–Wiles levels; T_G the Hecke algebra with maximal ideals m_G, m_{G,Q} (generated by the U^{(i)}_{ϖ_ṽ} minus products of the eigenvalues αγ, βγ); det : G → U₁; the twists f ⊗ θ (p = 2) and the exponent m_G.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26. The generator of m_{G,Q} is misprinted (sourceIssues E26); V₀ ignores the ramification of σ (E24).

items.name: The rings Δ_Q, R_Q and P_Q of §4
items.statement: For a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N: Δ_Q, with R_Q an O[Δ_Q]-algebra such that R_Q ⊗_{O[Δ_Q]} O ≅ R; P_Q the quotient of the pseudodeformation ring of G_{K,S∪Q} by the Taylor–Wiles conditions (at ṽ ∈ Q̃ the characters χ̄_{v,i} are α_vγ_{v,i} for i ≤ r and β_vγ_{v,i−r} for i > r), with its O[Δ′_Q]-structure; and the map P_Q → R_Q extending Corollary 4.3.

items.name: The component argument concluding Theorem 4.1
items.statement: Let p_∞, p′_∞ be the primes of P_∞ (and their images in R_∞) given by t and t′. By the vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group at the automorphic point, p_∞ is a regular point of Spec P_∞ lying on a unique irreducible component Z of Supp H_{G,∞}. For p odd, Spec R_∞ = Spec R_loc⟦X⟧ is irreducible and H_{D,∞} is faithful, so p′_∞ ∈ Z; for p = 2 the action of Ĝ_m^γ[2](O) is transitive on the irreducible components and gives the same conclusion. Hence t′ is automorphic and r_{π′,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} is automorphic after soluble descent.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.1, arXiv v2 pp. 35–37
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26.

items.name: The intermediate claim in the proof of Proposition 6.1
items.statement: There are ι, a soluble totally real E/F and a RAESDC π₀ on GL₂(A_E) with: (a) weight 0 and π_{0,v} an unramified twist of Steinberg at every v | p; (b) det r_{π₀,ι} = ε^{−1}; (c) r̄_{π₀,ι}(G_E) contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}) with a > a₀(p); (d) a place v₁ ∤ p with q_{v₁} ≡ 1 mod p and π_{0,v₁} an unramified twist of Steinberg; (e) Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic if and only if Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π₀,ι} is; (f) π_{0,v} potentially unramified for v ∤ pv₁. The proof passes through a prime q given by [Dim05, Proposition 3.8], an everywhere unramified finite-order χ over E with χ̄² det r̄_{π,ι_q} = ε^{−1} (the obstruction is 2-torsion in Br(F), with vanishing real invariants because ε·det r̄ is totally even), π_a from [BLGG12, Theorem 6.1.9], and a prime t with a tamely dihedral level raising.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.1, arXiv v2 pp. 46–48

routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: symmetric power functoriality for Hilbert modular forms by tensor-product functoriality lifting
routes.brief: Build on Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions), whose ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint but no layer plans the method that proves it for totally real fields. This Part II owns that method, from Newton–Thorne, 'Symmetric power functoriality for Hilbert modular forms', Ann. of Math. 203 (2026), no. 1 (arXiv 2212.03595v2): Clozel–Thorne's strategy of proving automorphy of Sym^{p+r−1} from residual automorphy of the two constituents of (1.1), with the twisted tensor constituent ^{φ_p}r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄ obtained by a new functoriality lifting theorem for tensor products. It is a sibling of SymmetricPowersByAnalyticContinuation and SymmetricPowerAutomorphyLifting (Newton–Thorne I and II) and of SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising (Clozel–Thorne, and Thorne 2024, route 17). Final theorems, as printed. Theorem 4.1: let F be totally real, r ≥ 1, p any prime, ι : Q̄_p → C, π, π′ RAESDC on GL₂(A_F) and σ RAESDC on GL_r(A_F) with (1) π, π′ of weight 0 and non-CM; (2) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}; (3) r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) ⊇ a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}), p^a > 5; (4) at each v | p, r_{π,ι}|G_{F_v} is ordinary (resp. potentially crystalline) iff r_{π′,ι}|G_{F_v} is, and both are potentially crystalline if p = 2; (5) at each v ∤ p, π_v is a twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is; (6) a perfect H ≤ (r̄_{π,ι} ⊗ r̄_{σ,ι})^{ss}(G_F) with an element of 2r distinct eigenvalues; (7) HT_τ(r_{σ,ι}) = {0, 2, …, 2r − 2} for every τ; (8) r_{π,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} automorphic and strongly irreducible; (9) r_{π′,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} irreducible — then r_{π′,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} is automorphic. Theorem 3.2: under the hypotheses of §3 (p ≥ 5, det r_{π,ι} = ε^{−1}, weight 0, Steinberg at p, tamely dihedral of order p at v₀ with q_{v₀} ≡ −1 mod p, image ⊇ SL₂(F_{p^a}) with a > a₀(p), potentially unramified away from p), SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1}, and σ as in Lemma 3.1, r_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι} is automorphic, attached to an ι-ordinary RAESDC representation of GL_{2r}(A_F). Theorem 5.5 (hypotheses S5-global) and Theorem 5.9 (hypotheses S5-local, with the conclusion p^a > M): assuming SP_{r−1}, SP_r and SP_{r+1}, there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π of GL_{2r}(A_F) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ ^{φ_p}r̄_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_{π,ι}. Proposition 6.1 and Corollary 6.2 (reduction to favourable local conditions over a soluble totally real E/F), Proposition 6.3 (residual witnesses for both blocks ⇒ Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π,ι} automorphic, via Thorne 2024 Proposition 7.4 and Theorem 7.5 without TP_r), and the induction proving Theorem 6.4 (SP_n for all n) and Theorem A, which ML.3 exports. Layers: (1) §3 setting: the hypotheses, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.3–3.8 with the auxiliary data v_a, M, X₀, K₀, u₀, the polarized s and the deformation problems 𝒮_{F₁}, 𝒮′_{F₁}, 𝒮′_{F₂}, 𝒮_{F₃}; (2) Propositions 3.9–3.14, the set 𝒫, the comparison diagram, and the conclusion of Theorem 3.2 (with s of type 𝒮_{F₁}); (3) §4: the reductions (10)–(16), π_K, σ_K, T, the rings R_Q, P_Q and the map P → R (Lemma 4.2, Corollary 4.3), the unitary forms of Proposition 4.6 with Lemma 4.5, Lemma 4.7, the patching Propositions 4.8–4.9 and the component argument; (4) §5: Lemma 5.3 and its square generators, Proposition 5.4, Lemmas 5.6–5.8, the propagation over Γ_π and Theorems 5.5 and 5.9; (5) §6: Propositions 6.1, 6.3, Corollary 6.2 and Theorem 6.4. Import: the P → R patching template of Newton–Thorne II from SymmetricPowerAutomorphyLifting (route 16); level raising and the automorphy lifting and residual automorphy of Thorne 2024 from SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising (route 17); ι-ordinarity, the ANT20/Tho15 residually reducible theory, BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1, ∼, potential diagonalisability and Newton–Thorne 2020 from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (route 5); local rings from LocalGaloisDeformationRings (L7, R08.2–R08.5); polarized and GL₂ global deformation problems and Taylor–Wiles primes from GlobalGaloisDeformations (G7, R04.3, R04.5); support and components from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra (R03.6); quaternionic forms and global Jacquet–Langlands from GL2ModularityLifting (R22.1, R22.2) and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer (R17.3, R17.4); Clozel's rationality and coefficient conjugation from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (AG2.0, AG2.6); image criteria and Dickson from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (G7, R01.4); Dimitrov's large image from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.3; the fields F(S) and ray class fields from ArithmeticGaloisDuality (R02.3) and the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap (layers 12–14); Hida families from OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting (R21.2). Respect the corrections recorded in sourceIssues. E24: the printed proof of Theorem 4.1 takes S = S_p ∪ Σ with Σ the ramification of π only, so it does not cover Lemma 5.8, where σ = Sym^{r−1}σ′ is Steinberg at v₀ and γπ is unramified there after base change; add σ's ramified places to S (unramified local conditions for r̃, D unramified and V₀ Iwahori there). E22: s must be shown unramified outside S_{F₁} (σ as well as π). E25: Lemma 5.7(4) needs residual irreducibility over F(ζ_t) for BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1. E1: in Proposition 5.4 only ℓ = 2 can fail the strict bound. E8: in Proposition 6.1, t must be prime to the conductor of π_a. Also E2, E16–E21, E23, E26–E29.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 5.4 and its proof, arXiv v2 pp. 39–40; the same step in the proof of Lemma 5.7, p. 42
sourceIssues.printed: PSL₂(F_{p^a}) contains an element of order t₁ (and t₁ ≠ p), and therefore that t₁ divides p^a − 1 or p^a + 1. In particular, we must have p^a > M. … this projective image either contains SL₂(F_{l^a}) for some l^a > t or is dihedral.
sourceIssues.correction: For an odd coefficient prime the printed strict bound holds; only the prime 2 needs a correction. From t₁ | ℓ^a ± 1: if ℓ is odd, ℓ^a ± 1 is even and t₁ is odd, so 2t₁ | ℓ^a ± 1 and ℓ^a ≥ 2t₁ − 1 > M. If ℓ = 2, one gets only 2^a ≥ t₁ − 1, and 2^a > M fails exactly when t₁ = 2^a + 1 is a Fermat prime with t₁ − 1 ≤ M. So Proposition 5.4 should read ℓ^a > M for ℓ odd and 2^a ≥ t_i − 1 for ℓ = 2 (or assume t_i > M + 1). Every use needs only the weaker bound: Theorem 5.9 is applied at p ≥ 5, where the strict bound holds, and uses l^b ≥ t₁ − 1 ≥ p^{a₀(p)} > max(4r, 5) at other primes; Lemma 5.7 uses l^a ≥ t − 1 > 4r + 1.
sourceIssues.reason: Equality p^a = t₁ − 1 = M is possible: for p = 2, M = 16 and t₁ = 17 (a Fermat prime), 2⁴ ≡ −1 mod 17, so PSL₂(F₁₆) contains elements of order 17, and nothing in the argument forces a larger field. The strict inequality is not proved in that case.
